patient.chief_complaint: Progressive confusion with melena and hemodynamic compromise
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. R. is a 61-year-old Hispanic man with severe alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD-Na 26) and prior grade III esophageal varices who was brought to the emergency department by his wife for progressive confusion and black tarry stools over the past 24 hours. The wife reports he was increasingly confused yesterday afternoon, could not recognize their grandchildren at dinner, and by this morning could not state his own name. She found bloody-appearing black stool in the toilet bowl multiple times. He has been drinking alcohol daily despite medical advice — wife confirms he drank yesterday. On arrival he is hemodynamically compromised with blood pressure 98/58, heart rate 122, and pale conjunctiva. His wife explains that he has been on lactulose and rifaximin for secondary HE prophylaxis following an episode 8 months ago. His rectal exam reveals melena. Ammonia is 194 µmol/L — markedly elevated. He also continues metformin despite cirrhosis.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade III-IV), alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD-Na 26) — precipitated by acute variceal hemorrhage with melena; metformin on med list is a separate concern (lactic acidosis risk).

optimal_actions.action: Obtain the core HE/precipitant panel: CBC, electrolytes/renal/liver function, glucose, ammonia, magnesium, lactate, INR/coagulation, CRP, TSH, zinc and blood alcohol/urine drug screen; add phenotype-specific tests only when indicated.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Metabolic, infectious, endocrine, nutritional or toxic precipitant, interpreted with ammonia as supportive rather than a severity marker.

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (Variceal hemorrhage management; restrictive transfusion; SBP empiric therapy).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering metformin (HOLD given AKI / lactic acidosis risk in cirrhosis), propranolol (HOLD during active bleed), lactulose, rifaximin; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.
Ascitic PMN to confirm or exclude SBP.

optimal_actions.action: EEG — confirm triphasic wave pattern; exclude NCSE. Triphasic waves are classic but non-specific (metabolic encephalopathies broadly); main role is exclusion of non-convulsive status epilepticus where the differential supports it.
Consult GI for urgent endoscopy + banding; hepatology; critical care — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

optimal_actions.action: Draw two sets of blood cultures, aerobic and anaerobic, before the first antimicrobial dose
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Growth identifies the organism and its susceptibility; a negative or pending culture does not exclude the diagnosis, and yield falls once treatment has started

optimal_actions.action: Perform a diagnostic paracentesis and send ascitic fluid for cell count with differential, protein and culture, inoculating blood-culture bottles at the bedside
optimal_actions.expected_finding: A polymorphonuclear count at or above 250 cells/mm3 establishes spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, which is a precipitant that must be treated whether or not fever or leucocytosis is present

optimal_actions.action: Send urine for microscopy and culture as part of the infection screen
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pyuria and bacteriuria identify a urinary source; a negative result removes it from the list of precipitants

useless_tools.rationale: Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: IV ceftriaxone for SBP prophylaxis in bleeding cirrhotic (proven mortality benefit) + treat SBP if present.
Hold metformin and propranolol; reassess once stable.
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not continue metformin in setting of AKI + cirrhosis + sepsis — lactic acidosis risk.
Restrictive (not liberal) transfusion strategy for variceal bleed.
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Bleeding cirrhotics should receive empiric ceftriaxone prophylaxis (any source) — proven to reduce 30-day mortality.
Variceal hemorrhage is among the top HE precipitants given the nitrogen load.

red_herrings.data_point: Metformin still on med list despite cirrhosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hold metformin in any cirrhotic with AKI or sepsis (lactic acidosis risk).
